spots.s: Ride the creaky 1877 cable car up Mt. Washington at golden hour — the skyline-at-the-confluence reveal is Pittsburgh's single best first-date move ($2.50, cash).
The string of free viewing decks along Grandview Ave — one of America's most famous city views, open and lit all night for the post-dinner stroll.
The photographers' overlook: a dead-center view straight up the rivers at the Point — quieter than Grandview and unbeatable at dusk.
Where the Allegheny and Mon become the Ohio — walk to the fountain at the tip, watch the paddlers and barges, and get the whole city in one panorama.
Baseball's most beautiful park — cheap outfield seats, the Clemente Bridge walk over, and the skyline lighting up by the seventh inning.
Seven floors on Pittsburgh's most famous son — the largest single-artist museum in North America, and the silver-cloud room is a playful date beat.
Room-sized installation art — Kusama infinity rooms, Turrell light pieces — in a North Side warehouse; art that hands you something to talk about.
Randy Gilson's riotously painted courtyard is the most colorful free stop in the city — and Randy's often there to chat.
The country's biggest indoor bird garden: penguins, free-flight rooms and sloth encounters — an easy, chatty afternoon date.
The renamed Carnegie Science Center: a real WWII submarine, planetarium laser shows and a giant miniature railroad on the North Shore.

spots.n: Carnegie Museums of Art & Natural History
spots.s: Dinosaurs on one side, old masters and the Hall of Architecture on the other — two world-class museums under one Oakland roof.
Thirty-one jewel-box classrooms — including an ornate Chinese Room — inside a 42-story Gothic tower; a cheap, quietly wow-y culture date.
Victorian glasshouse stuffed with seasonal flower shows and a tropical butterfly room — the city's most reliable impress-a-date stop, minutes from Squirrel Hill.
Free-admission art museum, Gilded Age mansion tours and a car-and-carriage collection on one leafy Point Breeze campus — café lunch included in the play.
Six floors of Pittsburgh in a Strip District icehouse — the original Mister Rogers set, a sports museum and enough steel-and-immigration story to fuel dinner talk.
The classic Pittsburgh Saturday: espresso and biscotti, Wholey's fish counter, Penn Mac cheese, sidewalk vendors — get there before 11a and graze.
Riverboat sightseeing cruises from Station Square — the sunset skyline sail is a lazy, scenic date that requires zero planning.
Rent a kayak at Venture Outdoors' dock behind the convention center and paddle the Allegheny past PNC Park — the cheapest way to see the city from water level.
The world's largest bicycle museum — 6,000+ bikes crammed into a free, gloriously weird North Side warehouse; catnip for anyone who rides.
An unassuming Troy Hill chapel holding some 5,000 relics — the largest collection outside the Vatican; a strange, hushed, only-in-Pittsburgh hour.

nightlife.s: DJ-owned Lawrenceville room built for dancing — open-format Saturdays plus monthly R&B night BLENDR (2nd Thu) and QRX's first-Thursday party; zero bottle-service attitude.
Gloriously divey Lawrenceville dance hall — the 80s/90s nights (90s Night with DJ Thermos) pack the floor with people who actually dance.
Former Moose lodge with pizza downstairs and a 450-cap ballroom upstairs — dance parties like the all-vinyl Title Town soul/funk night land here.
Pittsburgh's storied Saturday-night afterhours — serious house and techno until sunrise; the address lands in your inbox with the ticket.
Live jazz seven nights a week over Latin-Caribbean plates and proper cocktails in the Cultural District — downtown's easiest great-date default.
Seated room in the Strip's Terminal building with a real R&B/soul booking habit (Melanie Fiona, Souls of Mischief) — dinner-and-a-show without the arena.
Two-story Lawrenceville music hall leaning funk, soul and jazz — small enough that every show feels close.
Concerts inside a deconsecrated 19th-century church in Millvale — one of the coolest rooms in America to see a band.
Indoor/outdoor North Shore hall that hosts the city's biggest hip-hop dance party, Slappers N' Bangers, between national tour stops.
Tiny South Side listening room — singer-songwriters at eye level; a low-key show date with conversation built in before and after.
Prohibition-styled South Side speakeasy pouring some of the city's best classic cocktails — dim, unhurried and quiet enough to actually talk.
Downtown's showpiece cocktail bar — theatrical modern drinks a block from the Cultural District theaters; ideal pre- or post-show.
No-frills Blawnox roadhouse booking national blues acts — real music, cheap beer, zero pretense, fifteen minutes up the Allegheny.
Dueling-piano party bar downtown, Thu–Sat — singalongs turn into a dance floor by 10p; a reliable group-night opener.

eats.s: Pittsburgh's benchmark omakase — a serene Shadyside counter where the 7- or 11-course chef's choice is the city's blue-chip sushi splurge.
Glossy Market Square hand-roll bar pairing pristine nigiri with gin, sake and Japanese whisky — counter seats make a slick first date; reservations only.
New-in-2024 sushi on Grandview Ave — nigiri with the whole skyline spread out below; book a window table at dusk.
Shadyside's do-both sushi house: all-you-can-eat when you're hungry, a proper omakase when you're courting.
Roger Li's Lawrenceville izakaya — yakitori, sushi and sake upstairs until 2a on weekends; loud, fun and built for sharing plates.
Old-school Mt. Lebanon Japanese with four sushi chefs behind the bar — the suburban sleeper the sushi nerds respect.
Strip District fishmonger slinging surprisingly serious sushi at lunch — freshness is literally the business model.
A cult sushi counter tucked inside Wholey's fish market — watch it cut to order, eat it standing in the Strip, thank yourself.
Conveyor-belt sushi at SouthSide Works — gamified, low-stakes and fun; the easiest icebreaker dinner in town.
Lawrenceville shop from the Umami crew making noodles in-house on a Japanese machine — the chicken-pork double-broth bowl is the order.
Homey Shadyside ramen-ya on S Aiken — rich tonkotsu and gyoza that hit hardest after a cold-weather Frick Park ride.
Bright downtown Korean counter — build-a-bowl bibimbap and bulgogi that turned into a lunchtime institution.
Lawrenceville Thai in a walled brick garden that feels teleported from somewhere fancier — the prettiest warm-night date table in Pittsburgh.
Squirrel Hill's Korean-Japanese double act — sushi on one side of the menu, bulgogi and bubbling kimchi stews on the other; casual and beloved.

chinese.s: Chef Wei Zhu's James Beard-recognized Sichuan flagship — order from the authentic menu (mapo tofu, cumin lamb, proper málà heat); the reason Squirrel Hill is a Chinese-food destination.
The other great Sichuan house, up on Murray Ave — a deep menu of chile-oil classics; locals happily split loyalties between here and Chengdu Gourmet.
Hand-pulled noodles and soup dumplings made in the front window — Taiwanese-run, always packed, the beating heart of the Forbes Ave block.
Family-run Taiwanese on Shady Ave — three-cup chicken, oyster pancakes and boba; quietly one of the highest-rated Chinese kitchens in the city.
2025 opening from the Everyday Noodles team — homestyle xiǎoguǎn cooking on the same Squirrel Hill block; watch it become your regular.
Opened 2025 in North Oakland — har gow and siu mai handmade by Cantonese veterans; Pittsburgh finally has proper dim sum again.
Six private karaoke rooms above Forbes Ave with deep Chinese and English songbooks — the Squirrel Hill night-out closer, open to 2a on weekends.
Taiwanese-Hong Kong bakery café on Murray — egg tarts, taro cake and bubble tea for the post-dinner stroll.
Oakland's homegrown bubble-tea shop — fruit teas and cheese foam done right, steps from Pitt; the study-date standby.
Strip District Asian grocery institution — house-made tofu, live seafood and every sauce a Sichuan pantry needs.
The region's biggest Asian supermarket, expanded into the Strip in 2025 — produce, seafood and freezer dumplings by the cartload; two parking lots.
Dragon boats race the Allegheny every fall (Oct 10 2026, at Pittsburgh Brewing) — free to watch, rowdy to cheer, and crews welcome newcomers.

fishing.s: Cast the seam where the Allegheny meets the Mon — walleye, sauger and smallmouth stack along the confluence riprap. PA license required (trout stamp only for stocked waters).
75-acre county lake stocked with trout four times a year plus bass, crappie and channel cats — kayak-friendly and under half an hour out (trout stamp needed).
Three stocked ponds in one quiet county park — easy bank fishing for trout and panfish, ideal for a zero-stress evening session.
Downtown's concrete wharf is a legit cold-season sauger and walleye bite — park on the wharf, drop a jig, watch the barges slide by.
Current breaks below Lock & Dam 2 at Aspinwall concentrate walleye and hybrid stripers — classic three-rivers tailwater water minutes from the East End.
State surveys keep finding big walleye, white bass and smallmouth numbers below the Braddock dam — the Mon's most underrated stretch.
Stocked trout water threading through Etna and Shaler minutes from town — hit the early-season stockings with your trout stamp.
Bike-to bank fishing on the Mon right off the Three Rivers Heritage Trail — after-work catfish and smallmouth without leaving the city.
100-acre state-park lake west of the city — stocked trout plus bass and muskie, with a full day of trails if the bite dies; worth the drive.

3,225 acres north of the city where the PFBC stocks muskie, walleye, hybrid stripers and channel cats on top of native pike and bass — accessible pier at McDanels launch, kid-friendly fishing peninsulas at Bear Run and Park Road, and ice fishing in a hard winter.

Wilderness trout water through Ohiopyle State Park, fingerling-stocked end to end, with a nine-mile all-tackle trophy section from Ramcat down to the PA 381 bridge — or fish Meadow Run's delayed-harvest, artificials-only stretch.

biking.s: Real singletrack inside the city — Iron Grate's fast hillside descent, Roller Coaster's flow, ~20 miles of PTAG-maintained dirt five minutes from Squirrel Hill. The crown jewel.
The region's biggest ride: the Dr. J freeride line, a skills park and miles of stacked XC loops — Pittsburgh's busiest MTB scene.
Fast, flowy county-park network spiked with rock gardens and plunging descents — 30 miles of trails around a Tudor mansion.
Monroeville's county park hides a fun after-work singletrack network (plus the county's only ski slopes) on the east side.
Hillside loops under the Allegheny Observatory on the North Side — short, steep and blissfully uncrowded.
The destination day: ~30 miles of purpose-built, machine-groomed singletrack — the best trail network in the region, worth every minute of the drive west.
33 flat riverfront miles linking the North Shore, Strip and South Side — the everyday spin with skyline the whole way.
The GAP starts at the Point and runs 150 crushed-limestone miles to Cumberland — day-trip to Boston, PA, or dream bigger.
About 7 miles of very technical, rocky, rooty singletrack in Butler County — you work for every bit of downhill. Rideable in either direction.
Three well-marked, wide loops on Sugarloaf Mountain above Ohiopyle that combine into rides of any length — challenging climbs and fun descents, biggest on the loop around Sugarloaf itself.

social.s: 100+ vendor tents, food trucks and live music take over Murray Ave three summer Saturdays — the easiest talk-to-strangers night in the East End.
First- and third-Saturday socials at the Penn Ave dance studio — mini-lesson at 9:15p, then salsa, bachata and kizomba till 1a; no partner needed.
Second-Friday salsa night at the Bulgarian-Macedonian center — $12 with two free lessons up front and a genuinely mixed, friendly floor.
Free summer Wednesdays downtown — 30-minute beginner lesson at 6:30p, then hours of open-air dancing at the Cultural Trust's new green space.
Weekly salsa/bachata social run by the CrossBody studio crew — all levels, no partner required; check their calendar for which studio hosts.
Wednesday lindy hop at the Wilkins School in Regent Square — progressive lesson at 7p, social dance 8–10p; no experience or partner needed.
The Pittsburgh Marathon's free club — Saturday-morning group runs from rotating riverfront spots, every pace welcome, coffee after.
South Side board-game and retro-arcade café — pinball, pickup games and BYO drinks; the lowest-pressure hang on E Carson St.

social.n: City of Asylum at Alphabet City
social.s: Free Thursday-night jazz plus near-nightly readings and world-music shows at the North Side bookstore-venue — reserve a free seat, stay for conversation.
social.w: Thu nights + more · free w/ RSVP

social.s: BikePGH closes miles of streets to cars on summer Sundays — ride, run or stroll Downtown-to-Lawrenceville with half the city out.

Bachata 3 (No partner needed) Intermediate Bridging the gap between technique and application, this course focuses on providing reinforcement and improving intermediate to advanced partnerwork in the context… Tuesdays from 7p with Pittsburgh Dancing Meetup at Los Sabrosos Dance Co., Pittsburgh · $20 on Meetup.

Building upon the fundamentals learned in Salsa 1.5, we will deepen our knowledge of connection and weight transfer, and expand on social dance patterns. Thursdays from 6p with Pittsburgh Salsa Dance Meetup at 1918 Murray Avenue, Pittsburgh · no Meetup fee.

Bachata 1 (No partner needed) Beginner This course will cover the foundations of Bachata (basic techniques, body movement). Sundays from 5p with Pittsburgh Dancing Meetup at Los Sabrosos Dance Co, Pittsburgh · $20 on Meetup.

We focus on building strong lead/follow connections, frame, and the importance of timing, so you not only can dance with your classmates, but others as well. Thursdays from 7p with Pittsburgh Salsa Dance Meetup at 1918 Murray Avenue, Pittsburgh · no Meetup fee.

This is Intermediate play! Player limit is 12. There is only one court & only players signed up will be able to play. Mondays & Thursdays from 5:30p with Baker Park Intermediate Sand Volleyball at Baker Park, Upper Saint Clair · no Meetup fee.
We're a casual group of climbers who are also born to run! Mondays from 6p with ASCEND Pittsburgh Meetup at ASCEND South Side, Pittsburgh · no Meetup fee.

remote.s: North Side coworking at Nova Place, 100 South Commons. Fresh coffee, snacks & drinks, private phone booths, A/V conference rooms (2 hr/mo on Flex Unlimited), discounted Nova Place garage parking — included with the drop-in day — and gym access through Union Fitness. Short-term private offices for up to 4 run $85/day or $399/week, M–F 8a–5p.
remote.p: $30 drop-in day (parking incl.) · $50/mo (5 visits) · $135/mo unlimited · desk from $240/mo
remote.b: Quiet enough to focus, with a friendly social side

remote.s: East Liberty startup hub at 6401 Penn Ave. Every plan includes free parking, Wi-Fi and 100 prints a month, a phone booth, three conference rooms free to book, a kitchenette with coffee & snacks, plus expert office hours and founder programming. Members get 24/7 secure building access.
remote.p: Day pass (buy online) · Flex $125/mo (2 days/wk) · $225/mo full-time · desk $350/mo
remote.b: Plenty of desks, per member reviews

remote.s: On the 31st floor of One PPG Place, downtown, with floor-to-ceiling views. Complimentary coffee & tea, a large open kitchen and lounges, A/V, whiteboards, office supplies and a printer; tenants also get the building's fitness center and shuttle. Day passes run during staffed hours, M–F 8:30a–5p. No on-site parking; paid garages are a short walk away.
remote.p: From $35 day pass · meeting rooms from $60/hr
remote.b: Lively startup floor; regular mixers and happy hours

remote.s: Oakland coworking at 122 Meyran Ave, a short walk from Pitt and CMU, with sister spaces at 115 Atwood St and 1518 Forbes Ave in Uptown. The day pass covers a flex desk, phone booth and conference room. Across the sites: 1 GB internet, printers, mail service, drinks & snacks. Flex and dedicated members get 24/7 access and unlimited conference-room time; non-members pay $30/hr for the room.
remote.p: $25 day pass · $50/mo (4 days) · $150/mo flex desk · $250/mo dedicated
remote.b: Quieter than a coffee shop, per member reviews

remote.s: Lawrenceville coworking club at 3706 Butler St. Upstairs: a quiet library, a flex lounge, meeting rooms and a rooftop garden. Downstairs the Lobby Bar is open to anyone — coffee, espresso and a small breakfast menu in the morning, lunch at midday, then wine, beer and cocktails from 3p. Coworking members get 24/7 access and member rates at the bar.
remote.b: Café-like social floor, quiet library upstairs; evening pop-ups and rooftop happy hours

remote.s: One of three Pittsburgh COhatch spaces, at 2681 Sidney St in SouthSide Works. The others are Shadyside (5428 Walnut St) and the Waterfront in Homestead, which has a private movie theater and arcade games. The day pass covers coworking seats, phone booths, free coffee & tea and high-speed Wi-Fi, and one membership covers all three.
remote.p: $35 day pass · $50 business day (1 meeting-room hr) · 5 passes for $140
remote.b: Reviewers call the floor spacious; no peak-time data

remote.s: The flagship Carnegie Library at 4400 Forbes Ave, in the Carnegie complex in Oakland. Free Wi-Fi, and 2nd-floor reference study rooms and pods bookable on LibCal: up to 4 hr, one space per person per day. The open-air rooms have no ceiling, so they aren't soundproof; each seats six with floor and wall outlets. Lidded drinks only upstairs; food stays in the Yinz Coffee area on the first floor.
remote.b: Calm and quiet; peaceful reading nooks for deep focus

remote.s: The Downtown & Business branch at 612 Smithfield St. Free Wi-Fi, public computers and meeting rooms you request online in LibCal (staff review requests Monday–Saturday). Handy for a few hours near the Golden Triangle offices.
remote.b: Can be noisy; bring headphones; desks upstairs

remote.s: Bird-themed roaster-café on the bottom floor of an office building at 224 N Euclid Ave in East Liberty, open daily 7a–6p. Islands (2026) calls it quiet and welcoming, with reliable Wi-Fi and roomy seating — couches, armchairs and a large communal table — though outlets are somewhat limited. Snacks include vegan options.
remote.b: Quiet, outlet-rich room; weekday mornings least crowded

remote.s: Commonplace's North Side café at 1501 Buena Vista St in the Mexican War Streets, around the corner from the Mattress Factory. Islands notes free Wi-Fi, abundant outlets and ample seating at every Commonplace, with outdoor tables in summer. Other branches in Garfield, Shadyside, Squirrel Hill and Southside Works.

Pittsburgh-pride coffee shop at 2 E North Ave, at Federal St on the North Side, with wide windows looking onto Allegheny Commons. Local professionals polled by Table Magazine (2025) picked it for morning coffee, work and calls. Sister cafés include Station Square and CCAC's Allegheny campus.
remote.b: Small shop that gets busy, with lines; go off-peak

events.s: The Broadway musical of Nicholas Sparks' love story, with songs by Ingrid Michaelson, on tour at the Benedum — a ready-made date night.

events.n: Natural Woman: Sheléa Sings Aretha Franklin
events.s: Soul singer Sheléa fronts the Pittsburgh Symphony for an Aretha Franklin tribute, part of the PSO Pops series at Heinz Hall.
The old-school amusement park reopens for winter, lit up end to end with select rides running and holiday shows. Select dates only and a separate ticket — check the calendar and buy online.
The reunited Rush play PPG Paints Arena — one of the rock tickets of the year.

events.n: Phipps Holiday Magic! Winter Flower Show and Light Garden
events.s: Phipps' glasshouses dressed for the holidays plus the outdoor Light Garden after dark; open until 10–11p most nights, closed Thanksgiving and Christmas Day, 5p close on Christmas Eve. Timed tickets must be reserved ahead.

events.n: Dr. Seuss' How the Grinch Stole Christmas! The Musical
events.s: The touring holiday musical plays the Benedum over Thanksgiving week.
PBT's Pittsburgh-set Nutcracker at the Benedum — the final December for Terrence Orr's production before a new one premieres in 2027. A sensory-friendly show runs Sun 12/6.
Sunday Night Football at Acrisure Stadium. The game sits in the NFL's flex window, so the kickoff can move.
The Pittsburgh Symphony's holiday tradition with the Mendelssohn Choir of Pittsburgh, two weekends at Heinz Hall.
The AFC North's nastiest rivalry, at Acrisure Stadium the weekend before Christmas.
The Tony-winning musical about two helper robots who fall in love in near-future Seoul — a sweet date pick over New Year's week at the Benedum.
The Battle of Pennsylvania at PPG Paints Arena — the Flyers' first visit since the 2026 first-round playoff series. Early puck drop.

events.n: Greater Pittsburgh Lunar New Year Gala 春节晚会
events.s: The Pittsburgh Chinese Cultural Center rings in the Year of the Goat 羊年 on New Year's Day itself: lobby festivities, then music, dance, martial arts and traditional performances by artists from China and local groups at the Pittsburgh Playhouse.

events.n: Lupe Fiasco & Gym Class Heroes: Back to Basics Tour
events.s: Chicago lyricist Lupe Fiasco and Gym Class Heroes share a co-headline bill indoors at Stage AE on the North Shore; doors 7p, rescheduled from September with original tickets honored.
Friday-night ACC football under the lights at Acrisure Stadium as the Panthers host the Seminoles on the North Shore; students enter at Gate C and concessions are cashless.
The Oscar-winning Queen of Comedy plays four club-sized sets at the Improv at The Waterfront in Homestead: 7p and 9:30p Friday, 6:30p and 9p Saturday. Nearly sold out, so book ahead.
The dry New York stand-up settles into the Improv at The Waterfront for five shows: 7p Thursday, 7p and 9:30p Friday, 6:30p and 9p Saturday. An easy dinner-and-a-show date in Homestead.
Market Square's chalet-style holiday market: gifts, ornaments and hot drinks daily from 11a (to 8p Mon–Thu, 9:30p Fri–Sat, 6p Sun). Closed Thanksgiving; 3p close on Christmas Eve.
Downtown's holiday kickoff: tree lightings with rooftop fireworks at 5p and 7p, free stages from 4p, Daya headlining at Arts Landing at 8:30p, then the Zambelli finale over the Allegheny at 9:30p.
A rare Friday-afternoon kickoff at Acrisure Stadium the day after Thanksgiving, with Denver in town; lots open at 10a and gates at 1p, so the North Shore tailgate starts early.
Saturday-night hockey on Thanksgiving weekend as Toronto visits PPG Paints Arena — an Original Six draw and one of the bigger regular-season tickets Uptown.

Event: This will be a 6.5-mile moderate hike in Schenley Park. The hike will last approximately 2.5 hours, and there will be several early bail options for a shorter distance. Sunday from 12p with Beat the Blues Wellness Adventure Community at Schenley Park Overlook, Pittsburgh · no Meetup fee.

Smooth, flowing, and all about connection. Bachata Moderna blends the classic bachata basic with fluid movement, body rolls, and musical interpretation, and this class will show you how it all comes together. Sunday from 6:15p with Salsa Suave at The Eighty-Two Collective, Emsworth · no Meetup fee.

events.n: Over The Mountain - Social Climbing (Point Breeze)
events.s: Come join us for a morning climb! Meet at 10 a.m. Thursday from 10a with ASCEND Pittsburgh Meetup at ASCEND Point Breeze, Pittsburgh · no Meetup fee.

This beginner-friendly class walks you through the basics of On2 salsa, from your first steps to your first turns, in a space that's friendly, supportive, and judgment-free. Sunday from 5p with Salsa Suave at The Eighty-Two Collective, Emsworth · no Meetup fee.

West Coast Swing is fun, social, and seriously addictive! Come learn a dance that's all about connection, creativity, and having a great time on the dance floor. Tuesday from 7p with Pgh West Coast Swing at 82 Center Avenue, Emsworth · no Meetup fee.

events.n: WPAG: Board Games at the Four Horsemen
events.s: You can bring your own game or choose from their extensive board game library. Saturday from 12p with Western PA Gaming at Four Horsemen, Pittsburgh · no Meetup fee.

events.n: Board Games In Person Event at Yinz Coffeehouse in Bloomfield
events.s: Games To Be Played depend on what participants suggest or bring with them. Sunday from 12p with Board Gaming Geeks at YINZ COFFEEHOUSE Bloomfield, Pittsburgh · no Meetup fee.

iceskating.s: Downtown's holiday rink around a 60-ft tree in the glass-towered PPG Place plaza, which a 2015 expansion made bigger than Rockefeller Center's. It opens in mid-November and runs to early March, daily from 11a with later hours on weekends and over the holidays. Last season adults paid $12, rentals are on site, and Tuesday family nights add a free child ticket.

The city's open-air rink on Overlook Drive reopens in mid-November with sessions every day, adults-only skates Tue and Fri at 8:30p and Sat at 8p, Family Skate Nights and $1-off College ID nights. Adults $6, youth $3, rentals $3; capacity is 300. Closed Thanksgiving and Christmas, with single afternoon sessions on Dec 24 and 31.

One of Allegheny County's two outdoor rinks, off Pearce Mill Rd, typically open into mid-March, weather permitting. Public skate costs $6 for county residents and $8 otherwise ($10/$13 on Fri–Sat nights and holidays), rentals are $4/$5, and Friday mornings bring a senior skate. Season passes are gone; the county posts the opening date on its Parks Facebook page.

The county's south-hills outdoor rink on Corrigan Drive in Bethel Park shares North Park's prices: $6–8 daytime public skates and $10–13 on weekend evenings, with toddler-to-men's-14 rentals and free skate walkers on request. Sessions are timed, so staying for the next one means paying again. No racing, chains or carrying kids on the ice.

Mt. Lebanon's municipal rink in Mt. Lebanon Park, opened in 1977, with a 200-by-85-ft main sheet and a small studio rink. Weekday public skates are mornings ($7–9), weekend afternoons are $10 for adults, and the Friday TGIF Late Skate (7:40–10p, $13 with rentals) runs Sept 11–May 28. Rentals $4; skate aids aren't allowed at regular sessions.

The Penguins' practice home in Cranberry runs public skates on a monthly schedule posted on its site, plus themed sessions such as an Oct 31 Spooky Skate. Admission is $10, rentals $3 and skate walkers $5; a 10-visit pass is $90. Tickets sell online and close an hour before each session, and popular sessions sell out.

Robert Morris University's rink complex on Neville Island. Public skates (schedule updated Nov 4, 2026) run noon–2p Mon, Tue, Thu and Fri, 1:30–3:30p Saturdays and 7–8:30p Wednesdays; during the NCAA season the weekday afternoons move to the outdoor Stadium Rink. General admission $10, seniors $7, rentals $4. Call ahead, as times change.

A South Hills arena in Castle Shannon with two NHL-size rinks, open year-round, and cosmic and laser lighting at public skates. Admission is $10 (seniors $6, 5 and under free) and rentals $5; the Friday 7–9p session is a flat $15 including rentals. Buy 10 sessions and get 2 free.

skating.s: A flat, paved, traffic-free path along the Monongahela from the Schenley Park corner toward downtown, about 3 miles each way with views of the South Side bridges and Mount Washington. I-376 runs alongside, so it's noisy, and past the Smithfield St Bridge it switches to sidewalks. The Second Ave lot is free (3-hour limit 8a–6p, none on Sundays).

The North Side leg of the Three Rivers Heritage Trail: an easy, flat riverfront path past PNC Park, Acrisure Stadium, the Science Center and the marinas, with skyline views across the Allegheny and Ohio, running up to Millvale's Riverfront Park. Past the 40th St Bridge toward Aspinwall it turns to gravel, so turn around there.

skating.n: North Park Lake Trail skate loop
skating.s: A five-mile paved path around North Park Lake, the county's largest, starting from the 1936 Boathouse lot. The county widened this busy path for walkers and cyclists, and it follows Pearce Mill and Ingomar Roads before a quiet leg on one-way Lakeshore Drive, so expect car traffic beside you on parts of the loop.

The Montour Trail is mostly crushed limestone, but its Peters Township stretch, the township-run Arrowhead Trail, is about 3.5 paved miles from Route 19 to Brush Run Road. TrailLink notes a 0.4-mile on-road piece through a single-lane road tunnel and a busy SR 51 crossing, so this is the paved stretch to aim for.

The city's Schenley Park ice rink turns into a roller rink from late May through August, and inline and quad skates are both welcome. The 2026 season ran Wed and Fri evenings plus Thu/Fri mornings, with theme nights. Adults $6, youth $3, limited rentals $3; tickets are online only, capped at 200 skaters a session, weather permitting.

The Neville Island roller rink, with a maple hardwood floor, disco balls and inline as well as quad rentals ($4). Sessions run Wed–Sun: family skates $9–10, a Thursday-morning artistic skate to organ music, and $12 teen nights Fri–Sat where under-18s without their own skates need a parent. It also runs occasional 18+ adult skates.

Pittsburgh's member-run inline club ($20 a year) runs free adult group skates: Wednesday 6p lessons and a 6:30p advanced-beginner street skate in Shadyside/Oakland, plus Friday-evening and Sunday-9a intermediate city skates over bridges and river trails. The full season is May–Sept; off-season, Wednesdays move to Hazelwood Green.

BikePGH's car-free Sundays explicitly welcome skaters, with a 10 mph course limit. The 2026 season had two dates, 10a–2p: June 28 (about 2 miles through Downtown, Uptown and the South Side) and July 26 (3+ miles from Smallman St in the Strip to Butler St in Lawrenceville). The 2027 dates aren't posted yet.
